transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-21
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes (approx)
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Omar Ruiz (CSM), Lina Patel (Redwood SE); Evan Brooks (Northern Pipeline), Priya Shah (Eng Manager), Tomás Vega (DevOps)

Summary:
High-level kickoff for Sprint 0: network and access, staging topology, initial perf benchmarks, data residency and security check. Align on owners and immediate next steps for a two-week sprint to get a staging environment and run initial latency/cost baselines.

Topics discussed:
- Network connectivity (VPC peering, firewall rules)
- Deployment mode: Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (customer leaning to private/VPC)
- Security: SOC2, SSO, KMS integrations, audit logs
- Benchmarks: latency SLOs, throughput targets, sample prompt sets, token accounting
- Runbook and sprint cadence

Action items (captured here, see metadata for structured items):
See action_items field.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: okay hi everyone, thanks for joining. looks like we have folks from north— northern pipeline. can you hear me ok?
[00:04] Evan Brooks: yes yep hi maya, loud and clear. thanks for setting this up.
[00:07] Priya Shah: hi, thanks — appreciate the time.
[00:10] Maya Chen: cool, i'll kick off with a quick agenda — two goals for today: one, confirm what sprint-0 looks like (network, access, and a staging run); two, map owners and dates so we can get a perf baseline. lina will run through the technical bits.
[00:20] Lina Patel: hey everyone. so our typical sprint-0 for private/VPC installs has three parallel tracks: infra connectivity (vpc peering, routes, nat/egress), security and access (saml/sso, kms, audit log integrations), and runtime validation (small scale perf, model version pin, kv cache warmup).
[00:36] Tomás Vega: quick Q — when you say private install, are we talking full on-prem or a VPC-hosted private control plane? we want to keep data in our region and avoid cross-cloud egress.
[00:44] Lina Patel: good question. there are two main options: hosted private (Redwood managed control plane with customer VPC peering) or an on-prem bundle. for most customers the VPC option gives the right balance; data egress stays within your VPC, keys stay in your KMS. we can walk through the exact flow.
[00:57] Evan Brooks: we were leaning away from hosted public API — security team flagged it. so VPC-peered private control plane is our preference.
[01:03] Omar Ruiz: that's common. we'll get you a runbook for peering and the minimum firewall rules. Tomás, we'll need your peering CIDR and a list of egress IPs.
[01:12] Tomás Vega: ok i'll pull that. should i also open a case for IP-based allowlists or do you support FTPS? (laughs)
[01:17] Lina Patel: (chuckle) we don't do FTPS — IP allowlist is standard. i'll include NAT requirements and health-check ports. expect a checklist in the runbook.
[01:26] Priya Shah: on auth — our SSO requires SAML 2.0 with SCIM for provisioning. you support that?
[01:31] Maya Chen: yes — SAML SSO with SCIM provisioning is supported. Omar will handle SSO setup with you. one note, for RBAC mapping we'll need a short mapping table for roles (admin, dev, observer).
[01:41] Omar Ruiz: we'll send the SSO integration guide. quick note about audit logs — we can forward logs to your log collector or ship via S3 with encryption at rest. do you have a preference?
[01:50] Evan Brooks: prefer pushing into our Splunk cluster via a forwarder if possible, but S3 is ok for starters. must be encrypted with our KMS.
[01:58] Lina Patel: that's fine. we support KMS envelope encryption and can integrate with customer-managed keys. there might be some slight naming differences in the docs — i've seen KMS called "KM S" in some transcriptions — ignore that, it's KMS.
[02:10] Priya Shah: (laughs) okay noted. on the runtime side, can you describe what the perf validation will look like? we have strict latency targets: 95th pct under 250ms for short prompts.
[02:18] Lina Patel: for short-turn prompts that's ambitious, and it depends on model and batch. our recommended path: start with a small latency-focused test using a lightweight model variant to validate plumbing and KV cache behavior, then run a throughput window using your real prompt mix. we'll instrument token-level timing so you can see where time is spent — kernel exec, queuing, kv warmup.
[02:36] Tomás Vega: token-level timing — is that exposed in your console or via traces?
[02:40] Lina Patel: both. console dashboards show per-route token breakdown and latency histograms; we also provide span traces you can ingest into Jaeger/Datadog. note: sometimes the CSV export mangles headers, i.e., "kv_cache" becomes "kv chase" in auto-exports — these are minor quirks but we'll attach clean exports.
[02:55] Evan Brooks: haha the export quirks sound familiar. for benching windows, would you need us to run traffic, or can Redwood orchestrate synthetic traffic?
[03:03] Lina Patel: either works. usually we start with synthetic traffic to validate SLOs, then run a customer-driven realistic workload so we can measure real token distributions and caching benefits. if you can provide sample prompts that'd speed things up.
[03:14] Priya Shah: we'll deliver a 200-prompt set, maybe fewer, with redaction notes. security team requires that PII be redacted from staging datasets.
[03:20] Omar Ruiz: understood — include a doc about redaction rules; we can help sanitize prompts if you want.
[03:24] Maya Chen: quick commercial note — since you're on a short runway, do you want to discuss Dedicated reserved capacity later? not required for Sprint 0 but could come up.
[03:32] Evan Brooks: we want to avoid big capex. initially preferred private VPC with pay-as-you-go, but if costs look high we'll discuss reserved lines.
[03:39] Tomás Vega: can you surface likely cost delta between hosted and dedicated? ballpark is fine.
[03:43] Lina Patel: yes, we'll provide a small cost matrix. be aware quantization and batching parameters can swing per-token cost significantly. production throughput also matters — small bursty traffic benefits from reserved capacity less than steady throughput.
[03:55] Priya Shah: about compliance, we need SOC2 Type II evidence and an extract of your pen-test cadence for our risk team.
[04:01] Omar Ruiz: we'll share our SOC2 report and the pentest summary; there's a redacted version for non-legal stakeholders and a full package under NDA if needed.
[04:09] Evan Brooks: NDA might be needed — i'll check with legal.
[04:12] Maya Chen: sounds good. Lina, can you walk us through the specific ports and the minimal infra config?
[04:17] Lina Patel: sure — minimal: outbound HTTPS to a set of egress IPs, ports 443; ephemeral ports for health checks; VPC peering route tables need an /29 for the peering range. We'll include a sample CloudFormation and Terraform snippet in the runbook. for the load generator, allow tcp/8080 from our test agent if you want Redwood to run perf tests from our managed agents.
[04:38] Tomás Vega: we'll need the terraform snippet — we manage infra as code. also, any hints for container size if we decide to host an inference variant ourselves?
[04:45] Lina Patel: we can give recommended instance sizes. but for sprint-0 you're not doing self-hosted inference, correct?
[04:49] Evan Brooks: correct, not yet. focus is on private control plane and a Redwood-managed runtime in our VPC.
[04:54] Priya Shah: question — how do rollouts work? can we do canary by percentage or route-based?
[04:58] Lina Patel: both. rollouts support canary by weight and route-based pinning. you can also configure automatic fallback to a cheaper model variant if latency spikes.
[05:07] Priya Shah: fallback to cheaper variant — is that safe for quality-sensitive features?
[05:10] Lina Patel: it's a tradeoff. we recommend explicit A/B tests with traffic mirroring first. automatic fallback is for availability, not for final quality control.
[05:17] Tomás Vega: ok thanks.
[05:19] (short silence, people typing)
[05:25] Maya Chen: let's map owners and dates quickly. Omar, you'll take SSO runbook and audit logs. Lina, infra and bootstrapping docs plus perf plan. Maya will compile sprint plan and send the runbook. Tomás and Priya will provide peering info and prompt set. Evan will coordinate legal.
[05:42] Tomás Vega: got it. one more operational question — log retention windows, can we set retention per-environment? staging vs prod?
[05:48] Omar Ruiz: yes, retention is configurable per-tenant and per-environment in the console. default retention is 90 days, but we can extend for an additional fee or export to your long-term S3 bucket.
[05:58] Evan Brooks: we'll likely export to S3 and hook into our SIEM.
[06:01] Priya Shah: timeline check — our internal deadline is 12/12 to present a demo to execs. does that line up?
[06:07] Maya Chen: two weeks for sprint-0 gets you a staging baseline by ~12/05, then another week for production-ish hardening. 12/12 is tight but possible if action items land quickly.
[06:18] Evan Brooks: understood. we'll prioritize.
[06:20] Maya Chen: great. any final questions?
[06:23] Priya Shah: a small one — is there an official test harness you recommend for measuring tokenization differences across models? we've seen odd token counts.
[06:30] Lina Patel: yes, we'll share a tokenization test script. tokenization variance can cause cost deltas; we instrument token counts in the bench harness.
[06:38] Tomás Vega: perfect.
[06:40] Evan Brooks: thanks everyone.
[06:42] Maya Chen: thanks all. we'll follow up within 48 hours with the runbook and invite to the onboarding channel. recap in the meeting notes and action items are in the metadata.
[06:50] (meeting ends)

Notes about transcript quality: auto-transcript had occasional mis-hearings (e.g., "KV chase" for kv_cache, "KM S" for KMS). speaker labels were accurate. some timestamps approximated every ~15–30s.
